methodological_rigor.justification: This is a double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 RCT with 1:1 randomization via interactive response technology stratified by sex and liver metastatic status, with IRC-assessed PFS as the pre-specified primary endpoint per RECIST v1.1 — a rigorous design for the question. The Methods report Kaplan-Meier estimation with Brookmeyer-Crowley 95% CIs, Greenwood-formula event-free rates, stratified Cox models, and two complementary crossover adjustments (RPSFTM and 2-stage with bootstrap CIs) that appropriately address the 52.3% crossover rate; limitations of each (unmeasured confounders in 2-stage, treatment initiation differences in RPSFTM) are explicitly acknowledged. Weaknesses: this is a secondary 3-year analysis with no re-stated power/alpha for OS, biomarker/subgroup analyses are declared exploratory but no multiplicity correction is reported, missing-data handling is not described, and the OS HR 95% CI (0.51-1.05) crosses unity in the primary intent-to-treat analysis — a limitation partially mitigated but not resolved by crossover-adjusted analyses.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Design is an individual phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled RCT, mapping to Oxford LoE 1b. Clinical relevance is high: the trial addresses first-line treatment of recurrent/metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma — a disease with substantial unmet need, especially in Asia — using patient-relevant endpoints (OS, PFS, PFS after next-line therapy, safety) rather than only surrogates. The regimen is already approved by the EMA and Chinese NMPA on the basis of the parent trial, so these mature OS and biomarker data directly inform the durability and patient-selection questions clinicians face in practice. The B-cell signature finding adds a plausible, testable predictive-biomarker hypothesis that could refine selection beyond PD-L1 TC expression.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is the applicable standard and is explicitly invoked; the manuscript reports trial registration (NCT03924986), stratification factors, protocol and SAP in supplements, a patient-disposition figure, pre-specified primary endpoint, detailed TEAE/serious AE/immune-mediated AE tables, treatment exposure/dose intensity, and crossover accounting. Minor gaps: no explicit allocation-concealment statement beyond interactive response technology, no CONSORT checklist location referenced in the main text, and biomarker analyses lack a pre-specification/multiplicity statement. Data and code availability are not described in the manuscript text; while journal-specific statements may have been blinded out, no repository, accession, or code-sharing commitment is visible, so reproducibility of the GEP analyses rests on the referenced prior methods and supplements only.

novelty_literature.justification: This is a long-term (3-year) secondary analysis of the previously published RATIONALE-309 interim results (Yang et al 2023), confirming and extending the earlier PFS benefit with mature OS data and crossover-adjusted analyses. Empirical novelty is incremental: toripalimab (JUPITER-02) and camrelizumab (CAPTAIN-1st) have already demonstrated similar PD-1 + chemotherapy benefits in the same first-line R/M NPC setting, and international guidelines already recommend the approach. The more distinctive contribution is the exploratory GEP finding that a high B-cell signature is associated with enriched OS benefit (HR 0.41) while PD-L1 TC expression is not predictive — a biologically plausible, hypothesis-generating biomarker extension that nonetheless builds on prior NPC B-cell/TLS literature (Gong 2021; Lv 2023) rather than opening a new mechanism.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a clear IMRaD structure, informative figure captions that report event counts, medians with 95% CIs, and landmark survival rates, and a discussion that benchmarks results against JUPITER-02 and CAPTAIN-1st and candidly addresses the discordance between modest PFS and larger OS gains via immunologic mechanism and crossover. Limitations are explicit (Asian-only population, exploratory subgroups, inherent constraints of RPSFTM and 2-stage adjustments). The abstract is unusually structured — it opens with a question and bulleted key-points-style summary before the standard objective/methods/results — which is journal-specific formatting but briefly disorienting in the blinded form; terminology is consistent and acronyms are expanded on first use.

key_strengths: Mature 3-year OS and PFS from a double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 RCT with pre-specified IRC-assessed primary endpoint and clinically meaningful OS gain (45.3 vs 31.8 months)
Rigorous handling of 52.3% crossover with both RPSFTM (HR 0.56) and 2-stage (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.40-0.97) sensitivity analyses yielding concordant results
Clinically important question in a high-burden Asian cancer with directly practice-informing endpoints and regulatory relevance (EMA, NMPA approval)
Exploratory GEP identifies a biologically coherent, hypothesis-generating B-cell signature (HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.23-0.74) that extends predictive-biomarker thinking beyond PD-L1 TC expression
Thorough CONSORT-aligned reporting with disposition figure, protocol/SAP in supplements, and detailed safety including immune-mediated AEs
key_concerns: Primary ITT OS HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.51-1.05) crosses unity; OS claim rests on crossover-adjusted analyses that carry their own assumptions (unmeasured confounding, treatment-initiation differences)
Secondary long-term analysis of a previously published trial — empirical novelty is incremental and consistent with JUPITER-02 and CAPTAIN-1st
Biomarker and subgroup analyses are exploratory with no stated multiplicity correction or pre-specification detail for the B-cell signature cutoff
Asian-only enrollment (94.3% from China) limits generalizability to keratinizing NPC populations elsewhere
Data and code availability for the GEP analyses are not explicitly addressed in the visible manuscript text
chief_reviewer.rationale: A mature phase 3 RCT follow-up in a major cancer with pre-specified endpoints, rigorous crossover-adjusted OS analyses, and a novel biomarker extension is content commensurate with tier 1 oncology/general-medicine journals; minor revisions would address multiplicity, pre-specification of biomarker thresholds, and explicit data/code availability.
